memo: Clock: 29 days remain (due 2026-08-15); deadline not breached. Exemptions: none identified. Hours and proof: Screening confirms 88 qualifying hours per month from community-college education (more than half-time) — meets the 80-hour standard. Both documents on hand (enrollment letter and class schedule) are accepted proof. Member's concern that school 'doesn't count like a job' is resolved: REQ-ACTIVITIES explicitly lists 'attending school or an education program at least half-time' as a qualifying activity; DOC-SCHOOL confirms that half-time enrollment or more satisfies the standard by itself. Action: submit the enrollment letter and class schedule with the renewal form, checking the education box. No further work needed.
member_impact: Good news — your school is counting! Because you are enrolled in more than half of a full-time course load, the 80-hour work rule is met by your classes alone. You do not need a job or volunteer work on top of school. Here is what to send: your enrollment letter and your class schedule. Mail or submit them by August 15, 2026. That is it.
recommended_actions: Submit the enrollment letter and class schedule with the renewal response.
Check the 'education/school' box on the renewal form.

citations.quote: Qualifying activities include working for pay (including self-employment), attending school or an education program at least half-time, participating in a job-training or workforce program, and performing community service or volunteering with a qualifying organization.
An enrollment letter or class schedule proves education hours; half-time enrollment or more satisfies the standard by itself in most months.
Adults age 19 to 64 covered through Medicaid expansion must complete at least 80 hours per month of qualifying activities, unless an exemption applies.

findings.detail: Qualifying hours: 88 per month (88h education) — meets the 80-hour standard.
Every claimed activity (1) has an accepted document on hand.
